subject: ent
title: Rhinitis and nasal polyps

steps.tx: **Rhinitis** means inflammation of the nasal lining, producing blockage, watery discharge, sneezing and itching. **Allergic rhinitis** splits into seasonal disease triggered by pollens and perennial disease triggered by dust mite or animal dander, through IgE driven mast cell release that causes early sneezing and later congestion. Pale swollen turbinates and a nasal crease support allergy, while decongestant overuse, hormones, work exposures and non allergic triggers mimic it.
steps.say: An itchy nose with sneezing, watery discharge and blockage after dust or pollen exposure points toward allergic rhinitis. Seasonal symptoms follow pollens while year round symptoms follow dust mite or animal dander. Allergy releases chemicals from mast cells, so sneezing starts early and congestion builds later. Pale and swollen turbinates with a crease across the nose support the diagnosis. Daily decongestant sprays can themselves inflame the lining, so doctors always ask about spray overuse.

steps.tx: Care starts with avoiding known triggers and using a daily **intranasal corticosteroid**, aimed outward away from the septum for best effect. **Non sedating antihistamines** control sneezing and itching, while **saline irrigation** clears mucus as a useful extra measure. Selected severe patients with a proven dominant allergen receive **immunotherapy** by injection or under the tongue, which modifies the disease itself. Antibiotics have no role without evidence of bacterial sinus infection.
steps.say: The foundation of treatment is trigger avoidance plus a daily steroid spray aimed outward away from the midline. Antihistamines that do not cause sleepiness relieve sneezing and itching very effectively. Salt water rinses wash out mucus and help the steroid spray reach the lining. Patients with severe disease and one proven allergy may receive desensitisation injections or tablets under the tongue. Antibiotics do not help pure rhinitis, so doctors reserve them for proven bacterial sinus infection.

steps.tx: **Chronic rhinosinusitis** lasts beyond twelve weeks with blockage, discharge, facial pressure and reduced smell, grouped by whether polyps are present. **Nasal polyps** are pale grape like swellings that arise from the ethmoid lining and prolapse through the middle meatus, usually on both sides. They feel no pain when touched, unlike red tender turbinates. The triad of polyps with asthma and aspirin sensitivity is called **Samter triad**, while cystic fibrosis and fungal allergy explain selected cases.
steps.say: Sinus inflammation lasting beyond twelve weeks with blockage, discharge, facial pressure and smell loss defines chronic rhinosinusitis. Polyps look like pale grapes hanging from the middle channel of the nose, usually on both sides together. A polyp feels painless when touched, whereas the normal turbinate looks red and feels tender. Doctors remember the link between polyps, asthma and aspirin sensitivity because that combination changes management. Cystic fibrosis and fungal allergy cause polyps in a smaller group of patients.

vis.caption: Bilateral nasal polyps prolapsing from the ethmoid sinus. Image: Michael Hawke MD, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Polyp treatment rises step by step from saline rinses and **intranasal steroids**, including drops or high volume rinses that reach the sinuses. Severe swelling may need a short course of **oral steroids** to shrink polyps rapidly. When medicines fail, **endoscopic sinus surgery** opens the drainage pathways and restores ventilation. **Biologics** that block allergy pathways help selected patients with recurrent polyps and asthma in specialist care. Sinus CT scoring maps disease before surgery but never diagnoses simple rhinitis.
steps.say: Doctors start polyp care with salt water rinses and steroid sprays or drops that penetrate deep into the sinuses. A short course of steroid tablets can shrink severe swelling quickly when the nose blocks completely. Surgery that opens the sinus drainage channels follows only when medicines have failed adequately. Newer injected medicines that calm allergy pathways help patients whose polyps keep returning with asthma. A sinus scan maps the disease before any operation, although scans cannot diagnose simple rhinitis alone.

steps.tx: One sided disease changes the plan because an **antrochoanal polyp** from the maxillary sinus favours the young, while **inverted papilloma** or cancer favours older adults, so imaging and biopsy follow. Pain or swelling around the eye and any neurological sign mark **complicated sinusitis** needing urgent care. Bleeding as the main symptom points toward vascular or tumour causes instead. Smell loss after a viral infection often reflects lining injury and usually improves with structured **smell training**.
steps.say: A polyp on one side only is never routine, so doctors arrange imaging and a tissue diagnosis promptly. A growth from the maxillary sinus into the nose affects young patients, while warty tumours and cancers affect older adults. Pain or swelling around the eye with sinus symptoms signals spread beyond the sinuses and needs urgent care. Nosebleeds as the main complaint suggest a vessel or tumour cause instead. Smell loss after a viral infection usually recovers gradually with regular smell training exercises.

steps.tx: The endoscope shows a glossy pale **polypoid mass** filling one nasal cavity beside the **choana**. This matches the red flag step where a one sided mass needs imaging and biopsy to exclude **antrochoanal polyp**, inverted papilloma, or cancer. In the exam, link unilateral disease in youth with a maxillary origin and in older adults with neoplasia, and never biopsy a vascular tumour before scans.
steps.say: This endoscopic view presents a smooth pale mass that fills one side of the nasal cavity near the back opening. A one sided mass like this requires imaging and tissue sampling before any treatment. In a young patient it often indicates an antrochoanal polyp from the maxillary sinus. In an older adult the same picture raises concern for inverted papilloma or cancer.
